 Doomsday Movie Preparation
 Colleen Minnaugh 
 Student Contributor, Loyola University Maryland 
 This article is written by a student writer from the Her Campus at LUM chapter and does not reflect the views of Her Campus. You know that Lizzy McAlpine song that goes “Doomsday is close at hand, I’ll book the marching band to play as you speak, I’ll feel like throwing up”? That song is a perfect explanation for how I have been feeling these past few months as I slowly count down the days until December 18th. It’s getting closer and the closer it gets, the more I feel like throwing up. I am not quite ready to see my favorite characters inevitably get slaughtered (Bucky Barnes do not take any treacherous journeys!!!). However, since the movie is coming out soon and it is sort of going to be the end of a long saga of MCU films, my roommate and I have been slowly but surely making our way through a list of every film and show in preparation. So, I have decided to put together a comprehensive list (in release order) of all MCU projects that may or may not be important before watching Doomsday, along with little tidbits on whether I personally think they need to be watched. There are so many projects, and since it is a little less than a month out before the release, I know it would likely be impossible to get through them all. So, I will add a little star if I think that they really need to be rewatched, and a little sad face if I think they can be skipped for sure. The ones with no emoji next to them can be up to your own discretion! This is just my opinion, and since I have not yet seen Doomsday, I cannot say for sure which ones will be pertinent to the movie, but hopefully this list helps you plan out your movie marathon.

 Colleen Minnaugh is a senior at Loyola University Maryland. She is originally from Atlanta GA, and is a Writing major with a History minor. Writing and reading have been a huge part of her life since middle school; from AP Literature, to dramatic writing class, she has always known that writing would play a large role in her life.
 Colleen has been working at her local, all female owned and operated bookstore since she was fifteen years old, leading her to be exposed to many different kinds of writing styles and genres, but she quickly discovered that classic literature holds a very special place in her heart. From the stories told by the likes of Charlotte Bronte, Franz Kafka, to even the occasional contemporary author such as Sylvia Plath, Colleen is absolutely captivated by the beloved classics. 
 Colleen will mainly aim to write opinion based pieces on current events, pop culture, politics, book reviews, movie recommendations, and so much more! She will publish an article about every two weeks, and she hopes that you enjoy them each time!
